title: The Twenty-Third Psalm
lines: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.

title: Crossing the Bar
lines: Sunset and evening star,
And one clear call for me!
And may there be no moaning of the bar,
When I put out to sea,
But such a tide as moving seems asleep,
Too full for sound and foam,
When that which drew from out the boundless deep
Turns again home.
Twilight and evening bell,
And after that the dark!
And may there be no sadness of farewell,
When I embark;
For tho’ from out our bourne of Time and Place
The flood may bear me far,
I hope to see my Pilot face to face
When I have crost the bar.

title: Forever Loved
lines: You filled our days with quiet grace,
with open doors and gentle words,
the kitchen light, the steady hand,
the laughter that was always heard.
We carry you in all we do,
in every garden, every song;
and though we say goodbye today,
we hold you close our whole life long.

title: Eternal Rest
lines: Eternal rest grant unto {him}, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon {him}. May {he} rest in peace. Amen.
May {his} soul and the souls of all the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

title: An Irish Blessing
lines: May the road rise up to meet you.
May the wind be always at your back.
May the sun shine warm upon your face,
and the rains fall soft upon your fields.
And until we meet again,
may God hold you
in the palm of His hand.

title: The Lord’s Prayer
lines: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name; thy kingdom come; thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen.

title: A Covenant Prayer
lines: I am no longer my own, but thine. Put me to what thou wilt, rank me with whom thou wilt. Put me to doing, put me to suffering. Let me be employed for thee or laid aside for thee, exalted for thee or brought low for thee. Let me be full, let me be empty. Let me have all things, let me have nothing. I freely and heartily yield all things to thy pleasure and disposal.
And now, O glorious and blessed God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, thou art mine, and I am thine. So be it. Amen.

title: A Mighty Fortress
lines: A mighty fortress is our God,
a bulwark never failing;
our helper He, amid the flood
of mortal ills prevailing.
That word above all earthly powers,
no thanks to them, abideth;
the Spirit and the gifts are ours
through Him who with us sideth.
Let goods and kindred go,
this mortal life also;
the body they may kill:
God’s truth abideth still;
His kingdom is forever.

title: Nothing Can Separate Us
lines: What is the chief end of man? Man’s chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him for ever.

For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

title: I Am the Resurrection
lines: I am the resurrection and the life, saith the Lord: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.
I know that my Redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: and though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God.
Rest eternal grant unto {him}, O Lord; and let light perpetual shine upon {him}. May {his} soul, and the souls of all the departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

title: It Is Well With My Soul
lines: When peace, like a river, attendeth my way,
when sorrows like sea billows roll;
whatever my lot, Thou hast taught me to say,
It is well, it is well with my soul.
And Lord, haste the day when my faith shall be sight,
the clouds be rolled back as a scroll;
the trump shall resound, and the Lord shall descend,
even so, it is well with my soul.

title: The Our Father
lines: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name; thy kingdom come; thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.

title: The Hail Mary
lines: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

title: The Memorare
lines: Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who fled to thy protection, implored thy help, or sought thy intercession was left unaided.

Inspired by this confidence, I fly unto thee, O Virgin of virgins, my Mother; to thee do I come, before thee I stand, sinful and sorrowful. O Mother of the Word Incarnate, despise not my petitions, but in thy mercy hear and answer me. Amen.

title: The Twenty-Third Psalm
lines: The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. He hath set me in a place of pasture. He hath brought me up on the water of refreshment: he hath converted my soul. He hath led me on the paths of justice, for his own name’s sake. For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, for thou art with me. Thy rod and thy staff, they have comforted me. Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me. Thou hast anointed my head with oil; and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it! And thy mercy will follow me all the days of my life. And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord unto length of days.

title: De Profundis
lines: Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my voice. Let thy ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication. If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: Lord, who shall stand it? For with thee there is merciful forgiveness: and by reason of thy law, I have waited for thee, O Lord. My soul hath relied on his word: my soul hath hoped in the Lord. From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord. Because with the Lord there is mercy: and with him plentiful redemption. And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.
Eternal rest grant unto {him}, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon {him}. May {he} rest in peace. Amen.

title: Memory Eternal
lines: Give rest, O Lord, to the soul of Thy servant who has fallen asleep, in a place of light, in a place of refreshment, in a place of repose, where all sickness, sorrow and sighing have fled away.
Pardon every transgression {he} has committed, whether by word or deed or thought, for Thou art a good God and lovest mankind.
May {his} memory be eternal. Vechnaya pamyat. Aionia i mnimi.

title: Kontakion of the Departed
lines: With the saints give rest, O Christ, to the soul of Thy servant, where there is neither sickness, nor sorrow, nor sighing, but life everlasting.

Thou only art immortal, who hast created and fashioned man. For out of the earth were we mortals made, and unto the earth shall we return again, as Thou didst command when Thou madest me, saying: Earth thou art, and unto the earth shalt thou return. Whither we mortals all shall go, making our funeral dirge the song: Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
source: Kontakion, Tone 8 · Ikos of the funeral service

title: The Trisagion Prayers
lines: Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us. Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us. Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
All-holy Trinity, have mercy on us. Lord, cleanse us from our sins. Master, pardon our transgressions. Holy One, visit and heal our infirmities, for Thy name’s sake.

title: O Heavenly King
lines: O Heavenly King, the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth, who art everywhere present and fillest all things, Treasury of blessings and Giver of life: come and abide in us, and cleanse us from every impurity, and save our souls, O Good One.
Give rest, O Lord, to the soul of Thy servant, and make {his} memory to be eternal.

title: Prayer for the Departed
lines: O God of spirits and of all flesh, who hast trampled down death and overthrown the devil, and given life to Thy world: do Thou, the same Lord, give rest to the soul of Thy departed servant in a place of brightness, a place of refreshment, a place of repose, where all sickness, sorrow and sighing have fled away.

Pardon every transgression which {he} has committed, whether by word or deed or thought. For Thou art the resurrection, the life, and the repose of Thy servant, O Christ our God, and unto Thee we ascribe glory, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

title: Till We Meet Again
lines: God be with you till we meet again;
by His counsels guide, uphold you,
with His sheep securely fold you;
God be with you till we meet again.
Till we meet, till we meet,
till we meet at Jesus’ feet;
till we meet, till we meet,
God be with you till we meet again.

title: Taken Home to God
lines: Now, concerning the state of the soul between death and the resurrection — Behold, it has been made known unto me by an angel, that the spirits of all men, as soon as they are departed from this mortal body, yea, the spirits of all men, whether they be good or evil, are taken home to that God who gave them life.

And then shall it come to pass, that the spirits of those who are righteous are received into a state of happiness, which is called paradise, a state of rest, a state of peace, where they shall rest from all their troubles and from all care, and sorrow.

title: Sweet Unto Them
lines: Thou shalt live together in love, insomuch that thou shalt weep for the loss of them that die, and more especially for those that have not hope of a glorious resurrection.
And it shall come to pass that those that die in me shall not taste of death, for it shall be sweet unto them.

title: The Grave Hath No Victory
lines: And if Christ had not risen from the dead, or have broken the bands of death that the grave should have no victory, and that death should have no sting, there could have been no resurrection.
But there is a resurrection, therefore the grave hath no victory, and the sting of death is swallowed up in Christ.

title: I Am the Resurrection
lines: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.
Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.

title: Psalm 23
lines: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures; He leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul; He guideth me in straight paths for His name’s sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff, they comfort me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies; Thou hast anointed my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life; and I shall dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

title: Mourner’s Kaddish
lines: Yitgadal v’yitkadash sh’mei raba, b’alma di v’ra chirutei, v’yamlich malchutei b’chayeichon uv’yomeichon uv’chayei d’chol beit Yisrael, ba’agala uvizman kariv, v’imru: Amen.
Y’hei sh’mei raba m’varach l’alam ul’almei almaya.
Oseh shalom bimromav, hu ya’aseh shalom aleinu v’al kol Yisrael, v’imru: Amen.
May God’s great name be exalted and sanctified in the world created according to the divine will. May the One who makes peace in the heavens make peace for us and for all Israel. Amen.

title: El Malei Rachamim
lines: God, full of mercy, who dwells on high, grant perfect rest beneath the sheltering wings of Your presence, among the holy and the pure who shine like the brightness of the heavens, to the soul of {him} who has gone to {his} eternal home.
Source of mercy, shelter {him} forever in the shadow of Your wings, and bind {his} soul in the bond of life. The Eternal is {his} inheritance; may {he} rest in peace. And let us say: Amen.

title: Psalm 121
lines: I will lift up mine eyes unto the mountains: from whence shall my help come? My help cometh from the LORD, who made heaven and earth. He will not suffer thy foot to be moved; He that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, He that keepeth Israel doth neither slumber nor sleep.

The LORD is thy keeper; the LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand. The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night. The LORD shall keep thee from all evil; He shall keep thy soul. The LORD shall guard thy going out and thy coming in, from this time forth and for ever.

title: Eishet Chayil
lines: A woman of valour who can find? for her price is far above rubies. The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, and he hath no lack of gain. She doeth him good and not evil all the days of her life.

Strength and dignity are her clothing; and she laugheth at the time to come. She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and the law of kindness is on her tongue. Her children rise up, and call her blessed. Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.

title: Du’a for the Departed
lines: Allahumma ighfir la{hu} warham{hu} wa ‘afi{hi} wa’fu ‘an{hu}, wa akrim nuzula{hu} wa wassi’ mudkhala{hu}, waghsil{hu} bil-ma’i wath-thalji wal-barad.

O Allah, forgive {him} and have mercy on {him}; grant {him} well-being and pardon {him}. Honor {his} place of rest and make {his} entrance wide. Wash {him} with water, snow and hail, and cleanse {him} of sins as a white garment is cleansed of stain. Grant {him} a home better than {his} home, and admit {him} into Paradise.
source: From the funeral prayer (Sahih Muslim), plain rendering

title: Surah Al-Fatiha
lines: Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Alhamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin. Ar-Rahmanir-Rahim. Maliki yawmid-din. Iyyaka na’budu wa iyyaka nasta’in. Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim, siratal-ladhina an’amta ‘alayhim, ghayril-maghdubi ‘alayhim wa lad-dallin.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is for Allah, Lord of all the worlds, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgment. You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Guide us on the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who earn anger, nor of those who go astray.

title: Every Soul Shall Taste Death
lines: Every soul shall taste death, and you will be paid your full reward only on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever is kept away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has truly succeeded; the life of this world is nothing but a passing enjoyment.
Everyone upon the earth will pass away, and there remains the Face of your Lord, full of majesty and honor.

title: Remember {Him} in Your Du’a
lines: Please recite Surah Al-Fatiha and make du’a for the soul of our beloved {him}. May Allah forgive {his} shortcomings, accept {his} good deeds, widen {his} grave and fill it with light, and grant {him} the highest place in Jannatul Firdaus.
Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammad. Ameen.

title: Du’a for the Departed
lines: Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad.

O Allah, by the right of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, forgive {him} and have mercy on {him}; widen {his} grave and fill it with light; raise {him} among those You have blessed, and gather {him} with Muhammad and his purified household. Grant {him} a home better than {his} home, and admit {him} into Paradise.
Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad.

title: Surah Yasin
lines: Please recite Surah Yasin, Surah Al-Fatiha and the Salawat for the departed soul of {him}.
Every soul shall taste death, and you will be paid your full reward only on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever is kept away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has truly succeeded.
Everyone upon the earth will pass away, and there remains the Face of your Lord, full of majesty and honor.

title: Majlis-e-Tarheem
lines: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un. The family of {him} invites you to a Majlis-e-Tarheem for the departed soul, with recitation of the Holy Qur’an, Salawat and du’a.
Please remember {him} in your prayers. May Allah, by the right of Muhammad and his family, grant {him} the highest place in Paradise and give patience to those {he} leaves behind. Ameen.

title: Metta
lines: May you be happy.
May you be free from suffering.
May you be at peace.
May you be at ease.
May all beings everywhere be happy and free,
and may the thoughts, words and actions of our lives
contribute in some way to that happiness
and to that freedom for all.
source: The practice of loving kindness, plain rendering

title: The Five Remembrances
lines: I am of the nature to grow old; there is no way to escape growing old. I am of the nature to have ill health; there is no way to escape ill health. I am of the nature to die; there is no way to escape death. All that is dear to me and everyone I love are of the nature to change; there is no way to escape being separated from them. My actions are my only true belongings; I cannot escape the consequences of my actions. My actions are the ground on which I stand.

title: The Buddha’s Last Words
lines: All conditioned things are impermanent. Strive on with diligence.

Not in the sky, not in the midst of the sea, not in a cleft of the mountains, nowhere in the world is there a place where one is not overcome by death. Therefore cultivate what is good, and let the mind be at peace.

title: Worn-Out Garments
lines: As a person casts off worn-out garments and puts on new ones, so the embodied soul casts off worn-out bodies and enters others that are new.
For one who is born, death is certain; and for one who dies, birth is certain. Therefore you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.

title: Shraddhanjali
lines: With folded hands, we offer our heartfelt tribute to the departed soul of {him}. May {his} soul attain moksha, and may {he} rest in the lap of the Divine.
The family requests your presence at the Prarthana Sabha (prayer meeting) in {his} memory. Om Shanti, Shanti, Shanti.

title: Nanak Naam Chardi Kala
lines: Nanak naam chardi kala, tere bhaane sarbat da bhala.
O Nanak, through the Name may the spirit rise ever higher; and by Your will, may there be well-being for all.
Waheguru ji ka Khalsa, Waheguru ji ki Fateh.

title: Antim Ardas and Bhog
lines: With the blessings of Waheguru, the family of {him} requests your presence at the Antim Ardas and Bhog of Sri Sehaj Paath in {his} memory, followed by Guru ka Langar.
Please join us in prayer for the departed soul. Nanak naam chardi kala, tere bhaane sarbat da bhala.

title: Remember
lines: Remember me when I am gone away,
gone far away into the silent land;
when you can no more hold me by the hand,
nor I half turn to go yet turning stay.
Yet if you should forget me for a while
and afterwards remember, do not grieve:
for if the darkness and corruption leave
a vestige of the thoughts that once I had,
better by far you should forget and smile
than that you should remember and be sad.

title: Requiem
lines: Under the wide and starry sky,
dig the grave and let me lie.
Glad did I live and gladly die,
and I laid me down with a will.
This be the verse you grave for me:
Here he lies where he longed to be;
home is the sailor, home from sea,
and the hunter home from the hill.

title: Gone From My Sight
lines: I am standing upon the seashore. A ship at my side spreads her white sails to the morning breeze and starts for the blue ocean. I stand and watch her until she hangs like a speck of white cloud where the sea and sky come down to mingle with each other. Then someone at my side says, “There, she is gone!” Gone where? Gone from my sight, that is all. Her diminished size is in me, not in her. And just at the moment when someone says, “There, she is gone!” there are other eyes watching her coming, and other voices ready to take up the glad shout, “Here she comes!”

title: A Life Well Lived
lines: Not the years, but what we did with them;
not the words, but the ones we kept;
not the house, but who was welcome in it;
not the sleep, but the ones we loved while they slept.
Measure {him} by the room {he} made for us,
by the chair that was always ours,
and know that nothing {he} gave is gone:
we are the keepers of those hours.

title: Death Is Nothing at All
lines: Death is nothing at all. I have only slipped away into the next room. I am I, and you are you, and the old life that we lived so fondly together is untouched, unchanged. Whatever we were to each other, that we are still. Call me by the old familiar name. Speak of me in the easy way which you always used. Laugh as we always laughed at the little jokes that we enjoyed together. Life means all that it ever meant. It is the same as it ever was. Why should I be out of mind because I am out of sight? I am but waiting for you, for an interval, somewhere very near, just round the corner. All is well.

title: Tiny Footprints
lines: Tiny footprints, soft and small,
that never touched the ground at all,
have walked across our hearts instead
and left a path we’ll always tread.
We held you for a little while;
we keep you for a lifetime, child.
Sleep well, our darling, and know this:
you are the one we’ll always miss.

title: Suffer the Little Children
lines: But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.

title: Fearfully and Wonderfully Made
lines: For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother’s womb. I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

My substance was not hid from thee, when I was made in secret. Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.

title: I Shall Go to {Him}
lines: But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

title: A Little While
lines: We did not get the years we planned,
the first steps or the schoolyard gate;
we got a heartbeat and a name,
and love that would not, could not wait.
So short a while, so whole a love:
it fills the house, it fills the sky.
You were, and are, and always will be
ours, little one. We don’t say goodbye.

title: Held for a Moment
lines: We held you for a moment, and we will hold you for the rest of our lives. You were so small, and you changed everything: the way we see the morning, the way we say each other’s names, the way we count our family.
You are not a memory. You are our child, and you are loved, and you always will be.

title: Taps
lines: Day is done, gone the sun,
from the lake, from the hills, from the sky;
all is well, safely rest,
God is nigh.
Fading light dims the sight,
and a star gems the sky, gleaming bright.
From afar drawing nigh,
falls the night.
Thanks and praise for our days
’neath the sun, ’neath the stars, ’neath the sky;
as we go, this we know:
God is nigh.

title: I Have Fought a Good Fight
lines: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.
Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

title: The Soldier’s Psalm
lines: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.

He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler. Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day. For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.

title: Last Salute
lines: {He} answered when the country called
and wore the uniform with pride;
{he} stood the watch and held the line
with brothers, sisters at {his} side.
The flag is folded, Taps is played,
the last salute is slowly made;
the watch is over. Rest, and know
that what you gave will never fade.

title: Eternal Father, Strong to Save
lines: Eternal Father, strong to save,
whose arm hath bound the restless wave,
who bidd’st the mighty ocean deep
its own appointed limits keep;
O hear us when we cry to Thee
for those in peril on the sea.
O Trinity of love and power,
our brethren shield in danger’s hour;
from rock and tempest, fire and foe,
protect them wheresoe’er they go;
thus evermore shall rise to Thee
glad hymns of praise from land and sea.

title: Deep Peace
lines: Deep peace of the running wave to you,
deep peace of the flowing air to you,
deep peace of the quiet earth to you,
deep peace of the shining stars to you,
deep peace of the gentle night to you,
moon and stars pour their healing light on you,
deep peace to you.

title: The Parting Glass
lines: Of all the money that e’er I had,
I spent it in good company;
and all the harm that e’er I’ve done,
alas, it was to none but me.
And all I’ve done for want of wit,
to memory now I can’t recall;
so fill to me the parting glass:
good night, and joy be with you all.
Of all the comrades that e’er I had,
they’re sorry for my going away;
and all the sweethearts that e’er I had,
they’d wish me one more day to stay.
But since it falls unto my lot
that I should rise and you should not,
I’ll gently rise and softly call:
good night, and joy be with you all.

title: St. Patrick’s Breastplate
lines: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me, Christ in me, Christ beneath me, Christ above me, Christ on my right, Christ on my left, Christ when I lie down, Christ when I sit down, Christ when I arise, Christ in the heart of every man who thinks of me, Christ in the mouth of everyone who speaks of me, Christ in every eye that sees me, Christ in every ear that hears me.
Eternal rest grant unto {him}, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon {him}. May {he} rest in peace. Amen.
source: The Lorica of St. Patrick (C. F. Alexander, 1889) · traditional

title: Ar Dheis Dé
lines: Ar dheis Dé go raibh a {anam}.
May {his} soul be at God’s right hand.
May the Lord keep you in His hand and never close His fist too tight. May there be a road before you and a light to show the way, and until we meet again, may God hold you in the palm of His hand.

title: Oft, in the Stilly Night
lines: Oft, in the stilly night,
ere slumber’s chain has bound me,
fond memory brings the light
of other days around me;
the smiles, the tears,
of boyhood’s years,
the words of love then spoken;
the eyes that shone,
now dimm’d and gone,
the cheerful hearts now broken!
Thus, in the stilly night,
ere slumber’s chain has bound me,
sad memory brings the light
of other days around me.

title: Gone Fishing
lines: I’ve gone to fish a quiet lake
where mornings never seem to end,
where every cast is sure and true
and every stranger is a friend.
Don’t stand too long upon the shore;
the boat is small, the water wide.
I’ll keep the coffee hot, the line in,
and save a place here by my side.

title: Fishers of Men
lines: And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find.

title: A Fisherman’s Prayer
lines: Lord of the rivers and the deep, who walked beside the water and called the fishermen first: thank You for the early mornings, the quiet boats and the patient hours; for the one that got away and the ones that came home for supper.
Take {him} now to still waters, where the line is always tight and the day is never done, and keep a place on the bank for the rest of us.

title: Home From the Water
lines: The tackle box is put away,
the waders hang beside the door;
the boat is pulled up on the sand,
and {he} has gone ahead once more.
But every time the water’s calm
and mist lies on the morning lake,
we’ll feel {him} there, just out of sight,
in every cast we ever make.

title: I Will Lift Up Mine Eyes
lines: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the Lord, which made heaven and earth. He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.

The Lord is thy keeper: the Lord is thy shade upon thy right hand. The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night. The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul. The Lord shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.

title: Ask Now the Beasts
lines: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee: or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee. Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the Lord hath wrought this? In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.
The earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

title: The Last Hunt
lines: The frost is on the field at dawn,
the woods are still, the light is thin;
{he} walked this ridge a hundred times
and knew each trail, each stand, each wind.
Now {he} has gone on up ahead
to higher ground and older trees,
and when the wind moves through the pines
we’ll hear {him} in the morning breeze.

title: A Hunter’s Prayer
lines: Lord of the hills and the high timber, who made the elk and the whitetail, the wild turkey and the dawn: thank You for the cold mornings, the long walks in, the patience of the stand, and the meat on the table. Thank You for the friends made in deer camp and the stories told after dark.
Take {him} home now to the far ridge where the season never ends, and let the trail be easy under {his} feet.

title: The Final Round
lines: The last putt drops, the card is signed,
the clubs are cleaned and put away;
{he} walked the course {he} loved so well
and played it to the end of day.
Now somewhere there’s a morning tee,
a fairway wide, a sky of blue,
and friends who went ahead of {him}
are calling out, “We’ve saved a few.”

title: I Have Finished My Course
lines: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day.
Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us.

title: To Every Thing There Is a Season
lines: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted; a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak; a time to love.
He hath made every thing beautiful in his time.

title: A Golfer’s Prayer
lines: Lord, thank You for the early tee times and the long summer evenings, for the one perfect drive that kept {him} coming back, and for the friends who walked the course with {him}. Forgive the mulligans, count the gimmes, and let the scorecard show a life well played.
Give {him} a fair lie and a straight putt, and a seat at the table at the nineteenth hole.

title: The 19th Hole
lines: {He} always said the best part of the round was the nineteenth hole: the table, the stories, the friends who stayed. So raise a glass, tell the one about the shot that skipped across the pond, and laugh the way {he} laughed.
The round is over, but the company goes on. {He} is at the table now, saving us a seat.

title: A Firefighter’s Prayer
lines: Lord of the long night and the early call, who walked through the fire with Your servants and brought them out unharmed: thank You for every door {he} opened, every stair {he} climbed, and every family {he} brought out into the air. Thank You for the crew who had {his} back and the kitchen table where they laughed.
{His} last alarm has sounded and {his} watch is done. Take {him} home now, and keep those {he} loved.

title: Through the Fire
lines: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

title: The Last Alarm
lines: The tones drop one more time tonight,
the bay is quiet, the lights are low;
the turnout gear hangs on its hook,
the engine waits, and will not go.
{He} answered every call {he} could
and ran toward what the others fled;
now the last alarm has sounded, and
the watch is kept by us instead.

title: I Have Kept the Faith
lines: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day.
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

title: Well Done
lines: His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
Ye are the light of the world. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

title: Ride Free
lines: The engine’s quiet in the yard,
the helmet hangs beside the door;
the road {he} loved runs on ahead
past every mile {he} rode before.
So when you hear a motor sing
on some long highway, late and clear,
that’s {him}: the wind, the open road,
and not a thing on earth to fear.

title: Mount Up With Wings
lines: But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

title: The Road Not Taken
lines: Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
and sorry I could not travel both
and be one traveler, long I stood
and looked down one as far as I could
to where it bent in the undergrowth;
Then took the other, as just as fair,
and having perhaps the better claim,
because it was grassy and wanted wear;
though as for that the passing there
had worn them really about the same,
I shall be telling this with a sigh
somewhere ages and ages hence:
two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
and that has made all the difference.

title: A Rider’s Prayer
lines: Lord of the long road and the open sky, thank You for every mile {he} rode: the early starts, the back roads, the stops where the coffee was bad and the company was good. Thank You for the friends who rode beside {him} and the ones who waited at home.
{He} has ridden on ahead now. Keep the road smooth and the sun on {his} back, and bring the rest of us safely home.

title: See You Down the Road
lines: {He} never said goodbye at the end of a ride, just “see you down the road.” So that is what we say today.
Thank you for every mile, every story at the end of the day, and every time you looked back to make sure we were still there. See you down the road.

title: A Corn of Wheat
lines: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.
And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.
source: John 12:24 · Galatians 6:9 · Psalm 126:5-6, King James Version

title: A Cowboy’s Prayer
lines: Oh Lord, I’ve never lived where churches grow.
I love creation better as it stood
that day You finished it so long ago
and looked upon Your work and called it good.
I know that others find You in the light
that’s sifted down through tinted window panes,
and yet I seem to feel You near tonight
in this dim, quiet starlight on the plains.
Just keep an eye on all that’s done and said
and right me, sometimes, when I turn aside,
and guide me on the long, dim trail ahead
that stretches upward toward the Great Divide.

title: The Last Ride
lines: {He} rode out early, as {he} always did,
before the sun had cleared the eastern hill;
the gate is latched, the saddle’s on the rail,
the coffee’s on, the kitchen’s strangely still.
Somewhere the grass is green the whole year round,
the fences hold, the creek runs clear and slow;
{he}’s turned {his} horse toward that far pasture now -
happy trails, old friend, until we go.

title: A Farmer’s Hands
lines: {His} hands told the story: the calluses from the fence posts and the hay bales, the grease that never quite washed out, the gentleness with a newborn calf, and the way they folded at the table before every meal.
{He} fed people {he} never met. {He} watched the sky the way other people watch the news. The fields are quiet now, but the harvest {he} raised is in all of us.

title: {His} Shift Is Over
lines: The call light’s quiet, the chart is closed,
the hallway lamps are turned down low;
{he} gave {his} hands to strangers’ pain
and made the hardest nights less so.
{He} held the hands no one would hold,
{he} stayed on after the shift was done;
now someone else will walk {his} rounds.
Rest now. Your work is done. Well done.

title: The Nightingale Pledge
lines: I solemnly pledge myself before God and in the presence of this assembly, to pass my life in purity and to practice my profession faithfully. I will abstain from whatever is deleterious and mischievous, and will not take or knowingly administer any harmful drug.

I will do all in my power to maintain and elevate the standard of my profession, and will hold in confidence all personal matters committed to my keeping and all family affairs coming to my knowledge in the practice of my calling. With loyalty will I endeavor to aid the physician in his work, and devote myself to the welfare of those committed to my care.

title: I Was Sick, and Ye Visited Me
lines: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.
Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.

title: A Nurse’s Prayer
lines: Lord, thank You for the hands that took a pulse and held a hand in the same minute; for the nights {he} stayed late and the mornings {he} came in early; for every fever {he} watched, every family {he} comforted, and every patient who never knew {his} name but slept because {he} was there.
{His} shift is over now. Receive {him} as {he} received so many: gently, and with care.

title: Hands That Healed
lines: {He} spent {his} life taking care of other people, and {he} would not have had it any other way. {He} knew when to speak and when to sit quietly, when to bring the warm blanket and when to make the joke.
Thank you for every patient, every long night, and every time you came home tired and still asked about our day. We were lucky to be your family; so were they.

title: A Faithful Friend
lines: You met us at the door each day
with all the joy you had to give;
you asked for nothing but our love
and taught us how to simply live.
The house is quieter tonight,
your collar resting on the shelf;
but every room still holds your light,
and love like yours outlasts itself.

title: Until We Meet Again
lines: Run free now where the grass is tall,
where every path leads somewhere new;
no leash, no fence, no closing door,
and all the sky belongs to you.
Save us a place beside you there,
and listen for our step, and then
come bounding down the hill to meet us
when it is time to meet again.

title: Epitaph to a Dog
lines: Near this spot are deposited the remains of one who possessed beauty without vanity, strength without insolence, courage without ferocity, and all the virtues of man without his vices.
To mark a friend’s remains these stones arise; I never knew but one, and here he lies.
source: Lord Byron, Epitaph to a Dog, 1808

title: Paw Prints on Our Hearts
lines: Small paws that padded through our days,
a nose that found us when we cried,
a warm weight curled against our feet,
a steady friend who never lied.
You left your paw prints on our hearts;
they do not fade, they will not part.
Wherever love is kept and known,
you are still here, and still our own.

title: A Good Life
lines: You were loved every day of your life, and you loved us back without condition. You were patient when we were busy, gentle when we were sad, and glad every single time we came home.
Thank you for the walks, the welcomes and the quiet evenings. Thank you for being a good {dog}. Rest now, old friend. You did everything right.

title: Always With Us
lines: There is a chair that stays unfilled,
a bowl we cannot put away,
a leash still hanging by the door
as if you might come back today.
But you are in the morning sun,
the open window, the soft rain;
in every kindness we pass on,
you are with us, and will remain.
